papers.title: Ataluren treatment of patients with nonsense mutation dystrophinopathy.
papers.summary: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 174 males with nonsense mutation dystrophinopathy, ataluren 40 mg/kg/day slowed decline in walking ability and produced favorable trends in timed function tests, falls, and physical functioning over 48 weeks. Ataluren 80 mg/kg/day showed no effect on 6MWD, consistent with an inverse dose-response; the study was underpowered and dystrophin biopsy quantification was limited by poor sample quality.
papers.why: A randomized placebo-controlled study tested mutation-specific ataluren treatment in nonsense-mutation dystrophinopathy and measured functional outcomes.

papers.title: A Prospective Repurposing of Dantrolene as a Multitarget Agent for Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.summary: This paper primarily investigates repurposing dantrolene as a multitarget neuroprotective agent for Alzheimer’s disease. It reports inhibition of monoamine oxidase B and acetylcholinesterase, reduced amyloid-peptide aggregation, decreased oxidative stress in SH-SY5Y cells, and activation of the carnitine/acylcarnitine carrier; the only Duchenne muscular dystrophy connection is that dantrolene has previously been proposed for repurposing in that disease, without new DMD data in this study.
papers.why: Reports experimental repurposing of dantrolene in Alzheimer disease models with effects on calcium handling, oxidative stress, and neuroprotection, mechanisms that may transfer to dystrophin-deficient muscle.

papers.title: Deflazacort vs prednisone treatment for Duchenne muscular dystrophy: A meta-analysis of disease progression rates in recent multicenter clinical trials.
papers.summary: A meta-analysis of placebo-arm data from two phase 3 trials found that ambulatory boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy receiving deflazacort experienced significantly slower 48-week decline on several functional measures than those receiving prednisone/prednisolone. The largest adjusted difference was approximately 28 meters less decline in 6-minute walk distance, but corticosteroid assignment was nonrandomized, the follow-up was limited to 48 weeks, and the linearized NSAA difference fell below its proposed clinically meaningful threshold.
papers.why: The meta-analysis quantifies comparative functional outcomes for deflazacort versus prednisone/prednisolone in clinical-trial cohorts of boys with DMD.

papers.title: Calcium antagonists for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
papers.summary: This systematic review found five randomized or quasi-randomized double-blind trials of calcium antagonists in people with Duchenne muscular dystrophy. The trials did not provide evidence of a significant beneficial effect on muscle function; verapamil produced a between-group difference in ergometry-measured muscle force but also caused cardiac side effects.
papers.why: This systematic review reports randomized clinical-trial evidence directly in DMD for several calcium antagonists and their effects on muscle force and function, including adverse cardiac effects with verapamil.

papers.title: Increased dystrophin production with golodirsen in patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
papers.summary: In a phase 1/2 clinical trial, once-weekly intravenous golodirsen increased exon 53 skipping, produced internally shortened dystrophin, and increased dystrophin-positive muscle fibers in patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy carrying mutations amenable to exon 53 skipping. The study provides biochemical efficacy evidence at week 48 but does not establish functional or clinical benefit, which remained an unconfirmed longer-term outcome.
papers.why: The clinical trial shows that golodirsen induces exon 53 skipping and increases sarcolemmal dystrophin, validated through molecular and protein assays.

papers.title: Anaesthesia and neuromuscular disorders: what a neurologist needs to know.
papers.summary: This review identifies Duchenne muscular dystrophy as carrying an increased risk of perioperative or anaesthesia-induced rhabdomyolysis and sudden hyperkalaemic cardiac arrest. It states that the mechanism is unclear, that volatile anaesthetics might contribute but remains debated, and that proposed alternatives such as ketamine, propofol, opioids, barbiturates and benzodiazepines each have specific risks.
papers.why: Provides practical anesthesia-management recommendations relevant to DMD, including avoidance of succinylcholine and cautious dosing of nondepolarizing agents.

papers.title: Longitudinal effect of eteplirsen versus historical control on ambulation in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
papers.summary: In 12 ambulatory boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy and an exon 51-amenable dystrophin genotype, weekly intravenous eteplirsen was associated with slower 3-year decline in 6-Minute Walk Test distance and less loss of ambulation than in 13 matched historical controls. Respiratory muscle measures declined modestly but remained relatively stable, and treatment was generally well tolerated over approximately 3 years; interpretation is limited by the small sample, historical rather than concurrent controls, and unblinded extension treatment.
papers.why: This DMD longitudinal study provides three-year evidence that eteplirsen slowed the decline in ambulation compared with matched historical controls.

papers.title: Safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of casimersen in patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy amenable to exon 45 skipping: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-titration trial.
papers.summary: In a phase 1/2 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, once-weekly intravenous casimersen was generally well tolerated in 12 patients with advanced Duchenne muscular dystrophy whose DMD mutations were amenable to exon 45 skipping. Plasma exposure was approximately dose proportional from 4 to 30 mg/kg, renal excretion was the principal elimination route, and long-term weekly dosing showed little or no plasma accumulation; the small, advanced-stage population limited inference about clinical efficacy.
papers.why: This phase 1/2 trial established the tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and dose proportionality of casimersen for exon 45-amenable DMD.

papers.title: The pan HDAC inhibitor Givinostat improves muscle function and histological parameters in two Duchenne muscular dystrophy murine models expressing different haplotypes of the LTBP4 gene.
papers.summary: Fifteen weeks of oral Givinostat improved muscle function dose-dependently in two DMD mouse models carrying mild mdx/Ltbp4-insertion and severe D2.B10/Ltbp4-deletion backgrounds, although functional benefits were transient. In mdx mice, the highest dose also reduced fibrosis and increased myofiber cross-sectional area, while effects on fibrosis and cross-sectional area in the more severe D2.B10 model were limited or transient.
papers.why: Reports dose-responsive improvements in muscle function, fibrosis, and muscle cross-sectional area after givinostat treatment in two DMD mouse models with different LTBP4 haplotypes.

papers.title: Vamorolone targets dual nuclear receptors to treat inflammation and dystrophic cardiomyopathy.
papers.summary: The paper shows that vamorolone has a dissociative profile: it antagonizes the mineralocorticoid receptor while retaining glucocorticoid-receptor-dependent anti-inflammatory activity. In dystrophin-deficient mouse models, vamorolone prevented aldosterone-aggravated cardiac fibrosis, cardiac hypertrophy, hypertension, and dysfunction while avoiding several cardiac and metabolic effects observed with prednisolone.
papers.why: This mechanistic preclinical study shows vamorolone preventing mineralocorticoid-receptor-driven inflammation and cardiomyopathy in dystrophin-deficient mice while characterizing its receptor pharmacology.

papers.title: Recent Trends in Antisense Therapies for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.
papers.summary: This review summarizes antisense therapies for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, emphasizing AON-mediated exon skipping or gene knockdown to restore dystrophin expression or suppress inflammation. It reports four conditionally approved exon-skipping therapies, several investigational candidates with biochemical or early clinical benefits, and important limitations including weak clinical-outcome evidence, poor cellular delivery, renal clearance, trial holds, and toxicity.
papers.why: This review focuses on DMD antisense therapies and summarizes approved and investigational candidates using exon-skipping and gene-knockdown strategies.

papers.title: Clinical and genetic characteristics of female dystrophinopathy carriers.
papers.summary: In 154 female relatives evaluated for Duchenne muscular dystrophy/Becker muscular dystrophy carrier status, serum creatine kinase was positively correlated with disease carrier status and outperformed alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase as a noninvasive screening marker. MLPA combined with sequencing and muscle-biopsy immunohistochemistry identified dystrophin mutations or reduced protein expression, but negative genetic results could not exclude carrier status, particularly in suspected germline or somatic mosaicism.
papers.why: The study validates molecular and biochemical screening methods for dystrophinopathy carriers and reports CK performance data useful for DMD-family detection and research recruitment.

papers.title: Exon skipping and dystrophin restoration in patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy after systemic phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer treatment: an open-label, phase 2, dose-escalation study.
papers.summary: In an open-label phase 2 study, intravenous AVI-4658 induced DMD exon 51 skipping in all 19 participants and produced dose-dependent but variable dystrophin restoration, with seven patients showing increased expression. Dystrophin-positive fibres also showed restoration or increased expression of α-sarcoglycan and neuronal nitric oxide synthase, while high-dose cohorts had reduced muscle inflammation; no significant short-term muscle-function improvement or antidystrophin antibody induction was observed.
papers.why: A phase 2 DMD trial demonstrated safe systemic AVI-4658 treatment that induced exon 51 skipping and variable but measurable restoration of sarcolemmal dystrophin.

papers.title: The TREAT-NMD DMD Global Database: analysis of more than 7,000 Duchenne muscular dystrophy mutations.
papers.summary: The TREAT-NMD DMD Global database provides a global resource for analyzing 7,149 DMD mutations and their clinical and genetic frequencies. The analysis identified mutation classes and individual deletion patterns potentially addressable by premature-stop-codon read-through therapy or exon skipping, with exon-skipping applicability estimated for 55% of all mutations and 80% of deletions.
papers.why: The database contains 7,149 DMD mutations and supports diagnostics, trial planning, research, and identification of mutations eligible for stop-codon read-through or exon skipping.

papers.title: Nanoparticle delivery of Cas9 ribonucleoprotein and donor DNA in vivo induces homology-directed DNA repair.
papers.summary: CRISPR-Gold, a non-viral gold-nanoparticle delivery vehicle for Cas9 ribonucleoprotein and donor DNA, induced homology-directed repair of a dystrophin mutation in mdx mouse cells and muscle. In mice it restored dystrophin expression, reduced muscle fibrosis, and improved hanging performance without cardiotoxin, while producing minimal measured off-target genomic damage but a local increase in leukocytes.
papers.why: A nanoparticle delivery system co-delivered Cas9 ribonucleoprotein and donor DNA to correct a DMD mutation in mice with minimal off-target DNA damage.

papers.title: Local restoration of dystrophin expression with the morpholino oligomer AVI-4658 in Duchenne muscular dystrophy: a single-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-escalation, proof-of-concept study.
papers.summary: In a local proof-of-concept study, intramuscular phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer AVI-4658 induced exon 51 skipping and restored locally localized dystrophin in the extensor digitorum brevis muscles of boys with DMD deletions amenable to exon 51 skipping. The high dose increased dystrophin without treatment-related systemic or local adverse events or an anti-dystrophin immune response, but functional benefit was not studied and the low dose did not produce detectable dystrophin protein.
papers.why: This clinical proof-of-concept study shows that AVI-4658 safely increases local dystrophin expression in DMD patients with exon 51 deletions.

papers.title: Clonal isolation of muscle-derived cells capable of enhancing muscle regeneration and bone healing.
papers.summary: The paper identifies and clonally isolates mc13 muscle-derived stem cells from the mdx mouse model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy. These cells differentiated through the myogenic lineage and partially restored dystrophin after intramuscular or intravenous transplantation, while rhBMP-2 engineered mc13 cells also promoted osteogenic differentiation and healing of a skull defect in SCID mice.
papers.why: Reports isolation and transplantation of muscle-derived stem cells that promote regeneration and partial dystrophin restoration in mdx mice.

papers.title: Hypernitrosylated ryanodine receptor calcium release channels are leaky in dystrophic muscle.
papers.summary: In the mdx mouse model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy, age-dependent RyR1 hypernitrosylation is associated with calstabin1 depletion, increased sarcoplasmic-reticulum calcium leak, calpain activation, muscle damage, and impaired muscle and exercise performance. The paper reports that the channel stabilizer S107 prevented calstabin1 depletion, reduced calcium leak and muscle injury, and improved muscle force, fatigue resistance, grip strength, and voluntary exercise.
papers.why: Tests S107 in mdx mice and shows reduced calcium leak, muscle damage, and functional impairment through RyR1/calstabin-1 stabilization.

papers.title: Expression profiling in the muscular dystrophies: identification of novel aspects of molecular pathophysiology.
papers.summary: Expression profiling of human DMD muscle identified reduced dystrophin and ERK6 RNA, widespread mitochondrial gene downregulation, persistent expression of developmentally regulated genes, and infiltration by activated factor XIIIa+/HLA-DR+ dendritic cells. The study also shows that carefully replicated pooled-tissue expression profiling can detect primary biochemical defects and identify shared downstream mechanisms of dystrophin deficiency and α-sarcoglycan deficiency.
papers.why: This DMD tissue-expression study identifies persistent molecular alterations and potential disease markers using a reusable profiling approach.

papers.title: Eteplirsen in the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
papers.summary: This review describes eteplirsen as an exon 51-skipping antisense oligonucleotide intended to restore the DMD reading frame and produce shortened dystrophin in the approximately 14% of patients whose mutations are amenable to exon 51 skipping. Reported studies found increases in dystrophin expression but inconsistent assay results and no clear clinical benefit at 30 mg/kg/week; pulmonary decline appeared slowed, while efficacy, safety, and broader applicability remain limited.
papers.why: Reviews preclinical and clinical data for eteplirsen, an approved exon-skipping therapy that restores dystrophin translation in an estimated 14% of patients with DMD.

papers.title: Systemic AAV Micro-dystrophin Gene Therapy for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.
papers.summary: This review finds that systemic adeno-associated virus (AAV) delivery of abbreviated micro-dystrophin genes can produce body-wide muscle expression and improve pathology, force, cardiac function, and survival in murine and canine DMD models, but construct design and immune safety remain important determinants of efficacy. Early human evidence was insufficient or limited by immune responses and serious adverse events, although systemic delivery remains promising for whole-body DMD therapy.
papers.why: This review reports an existing systemic AAV micro-dystrophin strategy with preclinical efficacy and clinical trial development specifically for DMD.

papers.title: Precise correction of the dystrophin gene in duchenne muscular dystrophy patient induced pluripotent stem cells by TALEN and CRISPR-Cas9.
papers.summary: The study shows that TALEN- and CRISPR-Cas9-mediated exon skipping, frameshifting, and exon 44 knockin can correct a DMD mutation in patient-derived iPSCs and restore dystrophin protein after skeletal muscle differentiation. Exon 44 knockin was the most effective strategy because it restored full-length dystrophin, and genome-wide analyses found no severe nuclease-site-associated off-target mutagenesis, although a small number of clones had abnormal karyotypes and CRISPR knockin clones had a slightly higher indel burden.
papers.why: The study directly corrects the dystrophin gene in DMD patient iPSCs, assesses genomic integrity, and demonstrates full-length dystrophin expression after skeletal-muscle differentiation.

papers.title: Long-term evaluation of AAV-CRISPR genome editing for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
papers.summary: In the mdx mouse model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy, a single dual-AAV delivery of SaCas9 and two gRNAs excised Dmd exon 23, restored dystrophin, reduced serum creatine kinase, and maintained editing and protein restoration for one year after neonatal systemic treatment. Adult treatment elicited humoral and cellular anti-SaCas9 responses, while neonatal treatment avoided detectable responses, but AAV-CRISPR also caused unintended deletions, inversions, indels, transcript alterations, and AAV integrations that require further safety assessment.
papers.why: The study demonstrates durable dystrophin restoration after a single intravenous AAV-CRISPR treatment in a DMD mouse model while characterizing immune responses and unintended genomic and transcript alterations.

papers.title: Multiplex CRISPR/Cas9-based genome editing for correction of dystrophin mutations that cause Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
papers.summary: The study demonstrates proof-of-principle correction of dystrophin mutations in human DMD patient myoblasts using targeted CRISPR/Cas9 frameshifts or multiplex deletion of exons 45–55, restoring dystrophin mRNA and protein expression. Corrected cells also produced sarcolemmal human dystrophin after transplantation into immunodeficient mice, although editing efficiency, engraftment, delivery, off-target activity, and chromosomal translocations remain important limitations.
papers.why: Multiplex CRISPR/Cas9 editing restored dystrophin expression in DMD patient myoblasts and in vivo after transplantation, with one design potentially correcting up to 62% of DMD mutations.

papers.title: The 6-minute walk test and other endpoints in Duchenne muscular dystrophy: longitudinal natural history observations over 48 weeks from a multicenter study.
papers.summary: In 57 placebo-treated boys aged 5–15 years with nonsense-mutation Duchenne muscular dystrophy, the study provides 48-week natural-history data for 6MWD, timed function tests, and hand-held myometry. The 6MWD is presented as a clinically meaningful primary outcome measure: a change of approximately 20–30 m is clinically meaningful, while baseline values below approximately 325 m or 55% predicted are associated with greater subsequent functional decline and risk of loss of ambulation.
papers.why: This 48-week natural-history study validates and characterizes functional endpoints for predicting loss of ambulation in ambulatory DMD.

papers.title: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy: From Diagnosis to Therapy.
papers.summary: This review describes DMD as a dystrophin-loss disorder caused by DMD mutations and outlines molecular diagnostic approaches based on copy-number analysis, sequencing, next-generation sequencing, and transcript analysis. It surveys therapeutic strategies, including corticosteroids, small molecules, cell and gene therapies, utrophin upregulation, exon-skipping antisense oligonucleotides, and nanoparticle delivery, while emphasizing incomplete clinical benefit, delivery barriers, safety limitations, and the absence of a cure.
papers.why: The review describes clinically used molecular diagnostic approaches and DMD-directed antisense and delivery strategies for restoring dystrophin expression.

papers.title: Phase 2a study of ataluren-mediated dystrophin production in patients with nonsense mutation Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
papers.summary: In a 28-day Phase 2a open-label study, ataluren produced evidence of restored full-length dystrophin in muscle biopsies from boys with nonsense-mutation Duchenne muscular dystrophy, with quantitative dystrophin/spectrin increases in 23 of 38 patients and in vitro increases in 35 of 35 patient-derived myotube cultures. Serum creatine kinase decreased in most patients, but the study found no statistically significant short-term improvement in myometry or timed function tests and was limited by its open-label design, short exposure, small cohorts, and methodological variability in dystrophin quantification.
papers.why: This phase 2a trial directly tests ataluren in nonsense-mutation DMD and reports increased full-length dystrophin expression using a quantitative biopsy endpoint.

papers.title: Dystrophin gene mutation location and the risk of cognitive impairment in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
papers.summary: In 62 boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy, cognitive performance correlated with DMD mutation location and the cumulative set of affected central nervous system dystrophin isoforms. Classification by affected isoforms explained more FSIQ variance than mutation class, mutation size, or mutation location alone, although it explained only about 13% of variance and requires validation in larger cohorts.
papers.why: The same-disease cohort validates standardized cognitive testing and mutation-based classification of affected dystrophin isoforms as tools for predicting cognitive impairment.

papers.title: Src-dependent impairment of autophagy by oxidative stress in a mouse model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
papers.summary: In the mdx mouse model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy, increased Nox2-dependent oxidative stress activates a Src kinase–PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway that suppresses autophagic flux, autophagosome formation, and lysosomal biogenesis. Pharmacological inhibition of Nox2 or Src, or genetic p47phox deletion, restores these functions and improves skeletal-muscle pathology and contractile performance, although serum creatine kinase was not significantly reduced.
papers.why: Intervention experiments in the mdx DMD model show that inhibiting Nox2 or Src reduces oxidative stress, restores defective autophagy and lysosome formation, and improves histology and contractile function.

papers.title: Gene Therapy for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.
papers.summary: This review identifies DMD gene mutations and resulting dystrophin deficiency as the cause of progressive muscle degeneration, and concludes that mutation-independent AAV-mediated microdystrophin transfer is the most promising broad therapeutic strategy. Clinical and preclinical evidence remains limited by modest early efficacy, difficult dosing, anti-AAV and transgene immunity, potential repeat dosing, manufacturing constraints, and unresolved long-term safety risks.
papers.why: The review describes mutation-tailored exon-skipping approaches and AAV-mediated microdystrophin delivery, including large-animal efficacy data supporting DMD development.

papers.title: Inflammatory monocytes promote progression of Duchenne muscular dystrophy and can be therapeutically targeted via CCR2.
papers.summary: The paper identifies CCR2-dependent recruitment of inflammatory Ly6Chigh monocytes and accumulation of CD11bhigh macrophages as drivers of progression in dystrophic mdx mouse muscle. Genetic or pharmacologic CCR2 inhibition reduced pathological inflammation, fibrosis, necrosis, and contraction-induced damage while improving diaphragmatic fiber size and force generation, although these findings were obtained exclusively in mice.
papers.why: Genetic and pharmacological CCR2 inhibition reduced inflammatory macrophage accumulation and improved diaphragm pathology and strength in DMD models.

papers.title: Dystromirs as serum biomarkers for monitoring the disease severity in Duchenne muscular Dystrophy.
papers.summary: Serum miR-1, miR-133a, miR-133b and miR-206 were elevated in Duchenne muscular dystrophy, with miR-1 and miR-133b associated with respiratory function and several dystromirs associated with ambulation or disease severity. Eteplirsen restored dystrophin expression through exon 51 skipping, but the short studies did not show statistically significant changes in circulating or muscle dystromir levels after treatment.
papers.why: The study identified serum muscle microRNAs associated with DMD severity, respiratory weakness, and possible response to dystrophin restoration.

papers.title: Intra-arterial transplantation of HLA-matched donor mesoangioblasts in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
papers.summary: In an exploratory first-in-human trial, repeated intra-arterial transplantation of HLA-matched donor mesoangioblasts into five patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy was feasible and relatively safe, but efficacy was minimal. Donor engraftment was very low, donor-derived dystrophin appeared in only one patient, and most MRI and functional outcomes did not improve, although transient or sustained stabilization occurred in selected young ambulant patients.
papers.why: A first-in-human DMD trial showed that intra-arterial mesoangioblast transplantation was feasible and relatively safe, with transient functional stabilization and low-level donor-derived dystrophin in one patient.

papers.title: Animal models for muscular dystrophy show different patterns of sarcolemmal disruption.
papers.summary: The study shows pronounced, sometimes grouped sarcolemmal disruption and serum-protein influx in dystrophin-deficient mdx mice and subsets of DMD patient muscle biopsies, with some cardiac involvement. In contrast, laminin α2-chain-deficient congenital muscular dystrophy models and patients showed little or no grouped intracellular staining, supporting distinct mechanisms of sarcolemmal injury despite involvement of components of the same dystrophin–glycoprotein complex.
papers.why: The paper validates multiple muscular-dystrophy animal models and an Evans blue membrane-integrity assay, including direct data in DMD-relevant models and patients.

papers.title: Long-Term Safety and Efficacy Data of Golodirsen in Ambulatory Patients with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Amenable to Exon 53 Skipping: A First-in-human, Multicenter, Two-Part, Open-Label, Phase 1/2 Trial.
papers.summary: In a long-term Phase 1/2 study, golodirsen produced confirmed target engagement in ambulatory boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy amenable to exon 53 skipping, including increased exon skipping, dystrophin expression, and dystrophin-positive muscle fibers. Treatment was generally well tolerated, but small sample size, lack of a planned long-term efficacy control, and nonsignificant post hoc functional comparisons limit conclusions about clinical efficacy.
papers.why: Long-term clinical data showed that golodirsen increased dystrophin and had a favorable safety profile in ambulatory exon 53-amenable DMD patients, with exploratory functional comparisons to natural history.

papers.title: Genetic modifiers of ambulation in the Cooperative International Neuromuscular Research Group Duchenne Natural History Study.
papers.summary: In the CINRG-DNHS cohort, the SPP1 rs28357094 G allele was associated with earlier loss of ambulation primarily among participants receiving glucocorticoid corticosteroid treatment, supporting its interpretation as a pharmacodynamic biomarker of GC response. The protective LTBP4 rs10880 TT genotype was associated with delayed loss of ambulation in a population-stratification-controlled Caucasian subgroup, but was not significant in the overall unstratified cohort.
papers.why: This large natural-history study identified SPP1 and LTBP4 genetic modifiers of corticosteroid response and age at loss of ambulation in DMD.

papers.title: Use of capillary Western immunoassay (Wes) for quantification of dystrophin levels in skeletal muscle of healthy controls and individuals with Becker and Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
papers.summary: The study validates ProteinSimple capillary immunoassay (Wes) as a sensitive, reproducible method for quantifying full-length and trace dystrophin in human skeletal muscle biopsies, including samples from people with Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophy. Wes quantified dystrophin in 13 of 17 DMD samples and was more sensitive and quantitative than Western blot, supporting use of dystrophin as a biomarker in dystrophin-restoring clinical drug development.
papers.why: The study validates a sensitive, reproducible, low-sample assay for quantifying dystrophin as a clinical-trial biomarker in DMD muscle biopsies.

papers.title: Cardiac Pathophysiology and the Future of Cardiac Therapies in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.
papers.summary: This review describes dystrophin loss as the initiating defect in Duchenne muscular dystrophy cardiomyopathy, followed by membrane fragility, calcium dysregulation, oxidative and mitochondrial injury, nitric-oxide dysregulation, and fibrosis. It evaluates cardiac small-molecule therapies and gene-targeted approaches, identifying effective or promising interventions alongside cardiac null results, limited tissue delivery, incomplete correction, and substantial safety or durability concerns.
papers.why: The article catalogs current and investigational cardiac treatments and gene-directed approaches for DMD-associated dilated cardiomyopathy.

papers.title: Modeling and study of the mechanism of dilated cardiomyopathy using induced pluripotent stem cells derived from individuals with Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
papers.summary: Duchenne muscular dystrophy patient-derived iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes reproduced dystrophin deficiency, calcium overload, mitochondrial damage and apoptosis, and revealed a DIABLO–XIAP–CASP3 apoptosis network. Poloxamer 188 reduced cytosolic calcium, caspase-3 activation and apoptosis in these cells, while toxicity and patient efficacy remain unresolved.
papers.why: The study develops a patient-derived cardiomyocyte model and demonstrates that Poloxamer 188 suppresses DMD-relevant calcium dysregulation, apoptosis, and mitochondrial injury.

papers.title: Translation from a DMD exon 5 IRES results in a functional dystrophin isoform that attenuates dystrophinopathy in humans and mice.
papers.summary: The study identifies a glucocorticoid-responsive internal ribosome entry site (IRES) in DMD exon 5 that initiates a functional N-truncated dystrophin isoform in human muscle and cells. AAV1.U7-ACCA-mediated skipping of exon 2 activates this isoform in patient-derived myogenic cells and a Dup2 DMD mouse model, restoring dystrophin-complex components and improving muscle integrity, strength, specific force, and resistance to contraction-induced injury, with additional benefit from methylprednisolone.
papers.why: The study identifies a glucocorticoid-inducible translational bypass and demonstrates in cells and mice that it produces functional dystrophin and protects muscle.

papers.title: Open-Label Evaluation of Eteplirsen in Patients with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Amenable to Exon 51 Skipping: PROMOVI Trial.
papers.summary: In the open-label PROMOVI phase 3 trial, weekly intravenous eteplirsen in ambulatory patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy amenable to exon 51 skipping increased exon skipping and dystrophin expression over 96 weeks. Post-hoc mutation-matched comparisons suggested attenuation of 6-minute walk distance and percent predicted forced vital capacity decline, but the absence of a prospective mutation-matched untreated control limited causal interpretation.
papers.why: The multicenter PROMOVI study confirmed exon skipping and dystrophin increases with weekly eteplirsen and found attenuation of functional decline relative to natural-history controls.

papers.title: IL-1β- and IL-4-polarized macrophages have opposite effects on adipogenesis of intramuscular fibro-adipogenic progenitors in humans.
papers.summary: In human skeletal muscle, IL-1β-polarized and IL-4-polarized macrophages exerted opposite effects on fibro-adipogenic progenitor adipogenesis. IL-1β-conditioned medium suppressed adipogenesis and induced an inflammatory gene profile through ALK/Smad2 signaling, whereas IL-4-conditioned medium promoted white adipocyte differentiation, with macrophage–FAP proximity observed in DMD muscle.
papers.why: Using DMD patient muscle-derived cells, the study identifies macrophage-derived IL-1β and IL-4 pathways that regulate pathological fibro-adipogenic adipogenesis and provides candidate intervention targets.

papers.title: Genetic diagnosis of Duchenne/Becker muscular dystrophy using next-generation sequencing: validation analysis of DMD mutations.
papers.summary: The study found that targeted Ion PGM next-generation sequencing could detect all tested large DMD deletions, identify 50% of large duplications, and miss some difficult small insertions, yielding an estimated overall diagnostic rate of 92% for DMD/BMD. The authors propose using complementary MLPA and Sanger sequencing and increasing per-exon amplicon redundancy to improve diagnostic accuracy.
papers.why: The study demonstrates a validated high-throughput genetic diagnostic assay for DMD/BMD with an estimated 92% diagnostic yield.

papers.title: Validation of genetic modifiers for Duchenne muscular dystrophy: a multicentre study assessing SPP1 and LTBP4 variants.
papers.summary: In a multicentre cohort of 336 people with Duchenne muscular dystrophy, the LTBP4 IAAM haplotype was associated with delayed loss of ambulation, whereas the previously reported SPP1 rs28357094 association was not replicated. Corticosteroid treatment was independently associated with later loss of ambulation, supporting consideration of LTBP4 genotype when interpreting and stratifying future trials.
papers.why: This multicentre DMD cohort validates LTBP4 as a genetic prognostic modifier associated with prolonged ambulation and demonstrates a strategy for trial stratification, although the SPP1 association was not confirmed.

papers.title: Eteplirsen Treatment Attenuates Respiratory Decline in Ambulatory and Non-Ambulatory Patients with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.
papers.summary: Across three eteplirsen studies, 74 glucocorticoid-treated patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy and exon 51 skip-amenable DMD mutations showed statistically significant attenuation of annual percent-predicted forced vital capacity decline over 2–4 years versus matched CINRG DNHS external controls. The analysis supports respiratory benefit in both ambulatory and primarily non-ambulatory patients, although it used external natural-history controls rather than randomized controls and included interim data from study 301.
papers.why: The analysis reports that eteplirsen treatment is associated with clinically meaningful attenuation of annual respiratory FVC decline in exon 51-amenable DMD patients compared with natural-history controls.

papers.title: Safety and effectiveness of ataluren: comparison of results from the STRIDE Registry and CINRG DMD Natural History Study.
papers.summary: In a propensity-score-matched observational comparison, ataluren plus standard of care was associated with later loss of ambulation and later worsening of timed-function milestones than standard of care alone in patients with nonsense mutation Duchenne muscular dystrophy. Ataluren was generally well tolerated, but pulmonary and cardiac findings were inconclusive, and neither nonsense-mutation location nor stop-codon type predicted disease severity or treatment benefit.
papers.why: The comparative real-world study reports that ataluren with standard care delays functional deterioration in nonsense-mutation DMD and provides registry-based outcome evidence.

papers.title: Efficacy and Safety of Vamorolone Over 48 Weeks in Boys With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: The 48-week randomized VBP15-004 trial found that vamorolone 6 mg/kg/day maintained motor-function gains in boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy, while vamorolone 2 mg/kg/day provided less consistent maintenance across motor outcomes. Switching from prednisone to vamorolone reversed prednisone-associated growth slowing and declines in bone-turnover biomarkers and reduced several safety concerns, although adrenal suppression, early BMI increases, and other adverse events remained.
papers.why: This randomized placebo- and prednisone-controlled DMD trial provides direct 48-week efficacy and safety data for two vamorolone doses, including motor, growth, BMI, adverse-event, and bone-turnover outcomes.

papers.title: Long-term treatment with eteplirsen in nonambulatory patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
papers.summary: In an observational analysis of two identical twin patients with exon 51-skippable Duchenne muscular dystrophy, long-term eteplirsen treatment produced detectable dystrophin and was associated with relative stability of cardiac and upper-limb outcomes for up to 240 weeks, despite early loss of ambulation. The pulmonary trajectory was less stable, and interpretation is limited by the two-patient observational sample and open-label extension.
papers.why: The report provides longitudinal treated-patient evidence that eteplirsen produced dystrophin and was followed by relative stability of cardiac, pulmonary, and upper-limb function in two nonambulatory DMD patients.

papers.title: The "Usual Suspects": Genes for Inflammation, Fibrosis, Regeneration, and Muscle Strength Modify Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.
papers.summary: This review identifies and evaluates genetic modifiers of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), emphasizing pathways involving muscle inflammation, regeneration, fibrosis, TGFβ signaling, and muscle strength. Human association studies, mouse models, and in vitro experiments suggest that SPP1, LTBP4, CD40/TNFRSF5, ACTN3, and THBS1 variants can modify DMD severity or progression, although several associations are inconsistent across cohorts and remain exploratory.
papers.why: The review identifies validated genetic modifiers of DMD severity that can support prognosis, trial stratification, counseling, and therapeutic target selection.

papers.title: Detection of mutations in the dystrophin gene via automated DHPLC screening and direct sequencing.
papers.summary: The study demonstrates that automated denaturing high-performance liquid chromatography screening followed by direct sequencing can identify small DMD gene mutations missed by multiplexed PCR, finding likely disease-causative variants in six of eight male patients. The combined workflow increased the estimated overall DMD mutation detection rate from 65% to approximately 92%, but no likely causal mutation was found in two fully sequenced patients.
papers.why: The combined DHPLC and sequencing workflow detected likely causal mutations in six of eight DMD patients negative for large rearrangements and increased projected total detection above 92%.

papers.title: Dose-Titration and Open-label Extension Study of SRP-4045 in Advanced Stage Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) Patients
papers.summary: This is a first-in-human dose-titration and open-label extension study to assess safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of SRP-4045 in advanced-stage Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) patients with deletions amenable to exon 45 skipping.

papers.title: An Open-Label Extension Study of Edasalonexent in Boys With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary:
The GalaxyDMD study is a global Phase 3, open-label, treatment extension study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and durability of effect in long-term dosing of edasalonexent in pediatric patients with a genetically confirmed diagnosis of DMD. Patients who completed CAT-1004-201 or CAT-1004-301 or siblings of these boys from 4-12 years of age (up to 13th birthday) will be enrolled.

papers.title: An Open-Label Extension Study for Patients With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Who Participated in Studies of SRP-5051 (Vesleteplirsen)
papers.summary: The purpose of this extension study is to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of repeat administrations of SRP-5051 (vesleteplirsen) in participants with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) who participated in studies of SRP-5051.

papers.title: The Effect of a Muscle-mimicking, Fabric-type Shoulder Orthosis on Functional Movements of the Upper Limb in Patients With Neuromuscular Disorder
papers.summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to investigate the effect of a muscle-mimicking, fabric-type shoulder orthosis on functional movements of the upper limb in patients with neuromuscular disorder.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* What is the impact of the muscle-mimicking, fabric-type shoulder orthosis on upper limb functional movements in patients with neuromuscular disorder?
* Are there observable differences in upper limb function when the shoulder orthosis is worn versus when it is not?

papers.title: Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability of RO7239361 in Ambulatory Boys With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary: This is a multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study to assess the efficacy, safety and tolerability of two different weekly doses of RO7239361 in ambulatory boys with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD).

papers.title: Safety and Dose Finding Study of NS-065/NCNP-01 in Boys With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD)
papers.summary: The main objective of this study is to evaluate the safety of a high (80mg/kg) and low (40mg/kg) dose of NS-065/NCNP-01 delivered as an intravenous infusion in patients with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) amendable to exon 53 skipping. Additional objectives include tolerability, muscle function and strength, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics.

papers.title: Safety Study of Flavocoxid in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary: Objective of this study is to evaluate safety and tolerability of flavocoxid administered at the daily oral dose of 500 or 1000 mg/die for one year in DMD patients, alone or in association with steroids (deflazacort on alternate days) started at least one year before. The investigators will also perform a multidimensional clinical evaluation covering functional and muscle strength and quality of life (QoL)assessments.

papers.title: A Phase I/II Study of BMN053 in Subjects With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD)
papers.summary: The purpose of the study is to see whether BMN053 is safe and effective to use as medication for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) patients with a mutation around location 53 in the DNA for the dystrophin protein.

papers.title: Nebivolol for the Prevention of Left Ventricular Systolic Dysfunction in Patients With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary: The objective is to determine whether nebivolol, a beta-blockade drug, can prevent the development of heart disease in patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy aged 10 to 15 year-old.

papers.title: A Study to Assess Dystrophin Levels in Participants With Nonsense Mutation Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (nmDMD) Who Have Been Treated With Ataluren
papers.summary:
This study is designed to generate additional data on the effect of ataluren for producing dystrophin protein in nonsense mutation nmDMD participants. This study will evaluate dystrophin levels from participants with nmDMD who currently have been receiving ataluren for ≥9 months.

The study will have a single visit (Visit 1).

papers.title: Sedation During Muscle Biopsy in Patients With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary: This is an interventional study on Duchenne muscular dystrophy patients who will be receiving sedation for a muscle biopsy as part of another study.

papers.title: Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability Rollover Study of Eteplirsen in Subjects With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary: The primary objective of this study is to assess the ongoing efficacy, safety, and tolerability of an additional 212 weeks of treatment with eteplirsen injection in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) subjects who have successfully completed the 28 week eteplirsen study: Study 4658-us-201. This study will also evaluate the correlation between biomarkers for DMD and the clinical status of participating DMD subjects.

papers.title: A Gene Transfer Therapy to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of Delandistrogene Moxeparvovec (SRP-9001) Following Therapeutic Plasma Exchange (Plasmapheresis) in Participants With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) and Pre-existing Antibodies to AAVrh74
papers.summary: This is a gene transfer therapy study evaluating the safety of and delandistrogene moxeparvovec dystrophin protein expression from delandistrogene moxeparvovec following therapeutic plasma exchange (plasmapheresis) in ambulatory male participants with DMD and pre-existing antibodies to AAVrh74 over a period of 59 weeks.

papers.title: Tamoxifen in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary:
A randomised, double blind, placebo controlled, 48-week clinical trial with a core population (group A) of 79 ambulant 6.5 to 12 years old Duchenne's muscular dystrophy (DMD) patients that are under stable standard treatment of care with glucocorticoids. Furthermore, the investigators plan to include 6-20 non-ambulant patients who do not receive glucocorticoids (as parallel group B), 10 to 16 years old, to obtain efficacy and safety data in a broader DMD population. All patients will receive 20 mg of tamoxifen (TAM) or placebo once daily during 48 weeks.

papers.title: To Compare the Pharmacokinetics Profiles of ISO 20, IBU 200 and IBU Plus ISO Combinations 200 + 20
papers.summary:
This study will evaluate the pharmacokinetics plasma profile of 3 treatments: ISO 20, IBU 200 and IBU and ISO combinations (200 +20) given in single dose.

This study is being conducted to support the submission for new indication in treatment of the combinations of Isosorbide Dinitrate and Ibuprofen as a treatment for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

papers.title: Safety and Dystrophin Expression of SPOT-03 in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) Patients
papers.summary: The primary objective of this study is to evaluate the safety and tolerability of SPOT-03 administered by intravenous (IV) infusion to DMD patients. In addition, this study will preliminarily investigate the changes in dystrophin nucleic acid concentration, dystrophin protein expression and engraftment, anti-dystrophin antibodies and cytokine profiles, as well as fat tissue mas and lean tissue mass following SPOT-03 administrations.

papers.title: Gene Transfer Clinical Trial for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Using rAAVrh74.MCK.GALGT2
papers.summary: The proposed clinical trial study of rAAVrh74.MCK.GALGT2 for duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) patients that will involve direct intramuscular injection to the extensor digitorum brevis muscle (EDB).

papers.title: Phase 2 Study of EDG-5506 in Becker Muscular Dystrophy (GRAND CANYON)
papers.summary: A study of sevasemten (EDG-5506) in Becker muscular dystrophy (known as CANYON) and pivotal cohort (known as GRAND CANYON). The EDG-5506-201 CANYON study was expanded to include an additional 175 adult participants in a cohort called GRAND CANYON, that is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of sevasemten in adults with Becker.

papers.title: Digital Monitoring of Upper Limb Function in Non-Ambulant DMD
papers.summary:
Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) is a rare genetic disorder caused by the absence of dystrophin, leading to progressive muscle degeneration. Symptoms typically begin in early childhood and result in loss of ambulation by early adolescence, followed by cardiorespiratory complications. Although early treatment, including corticosteroids and emerging therapies, can slow disease progression, sensitive tools to monitor functional decline-particularly in non-ambulant patients-remain limited.

Current assessments rely primarily on clinical scales and hospital-based evaluations, which may not detect

papers.title: A Study to Evaluate the Safety and Tolerability of Rituxan in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary:
1. Study population:It is applicable to male participants with genetically confirmed and clinically confirmed Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), aged between 6 and 10 years.
2. Research period:The main research period of this clinical study is one year. Participants were tested during the baseline period and were followed up on days 0, 7, 14, 21, 60, 120, 200, and 360.
3. Exploratory indicators：MR Of both thighs, quantitatively calculating the muscle fat replacement indicators of the buttocks and proximal thighs；Patient Self-Rating Scale, Caregiver Self-Rating Scale.

papers.title: A Gene Transfer Therapy Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of Delandistrogene Moxeparvovec (SRP-9001) in Non-Ambulatory and Ambulatory Participants With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD)
papers.summary: The study will evaluate the safety and efficacy of delandistrogene moxeparvovec gene transfer therapy in non-ambulatory and ambulatory males with DMD. This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled 2-part study. Participants will be in the study for approximately 128 weeks. All participants will have the opportunity to receive intravenous (IV) delandistrogene moxeparvovec in either Part 1 or Part 2.

papers.title: The Safety, Efficacy and Tolerability of Remote Ischemic Preconditioning as a Therapy to DMD
papers.summary:
Background: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is an X chromosome recessive hereditary disease and mainly characterized by progressive muscle weakness and atrophy. Glucocorticoid is the only proven effective medicine,while side effects limit its use. Recent studies have shown that the vascular density in the DMD patients' muscle is decreased,so muscle are in ischemic and anoxic. Remote ischemic preconditioning(RIPC) can improve the capable of resistanting ischemia and hypoxia and maybe a potential therapy for DMD patients.
