papers.title: Extension Study of BMN 044 in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD)
papers.summary: The aim of this study is to provide continuing access to BMN 044 treatment for subjects previously treated with BMN 044. The information gained from this study is expected to further characterize the efficacy and safety of BMN 044 over a longer treatment period.

papers.title: L-citrulline and Metformin in Becker's Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary: The purpose of the study is to compare the effects of L-citrulline and metformin and their combination therapy on muscle function and force in patients with Becker muscular dystrophy (BMD).

papers.title: An Extension Study to Assess Vamorolone in Boys With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD)
papers.summary: The main purposes of this study are to see if it is safe to use a new medication called vamorolone for more than two weeks in children with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), to see if vamorolone works for the treatment for DMD, and to see how any potential side effects compare to those seen in boys using steroids.

papers.title: Therapeutic Potential for Aldosterone Inhibition in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary: The study is to demonstrate non-inferiority of spironolactone vs. eplerenone in preserving cardiac and pulmonary function in patients with preserved LV ejection fraction. Males with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) confirmed clinically and by mutation analysis will be enrolled. Subjects will be randomized to either eplerenone or spironolactone. Subjects will use a drug diary to record daily compliance of taking the study medication as well as any concerns they may have during the study period. Subjects will undergo cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) and pulmonary function tests (PFT) at

papers.title: Study of AOC 1044 in Healthy Adult Volunteers and Participants With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) Mutations Amenable to Exon 44 Skipping
papers.summary:
AOC 1044-CS1 (EXPLORE44) is a Phase 1/2 study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamic effects of single and multiple ascending doses of AOC 1044 in healthy adult volunteers and participants with DMD mutations amenable to exon 44 skipping.

Part A is a single dose design with multiple cohorts (dose levels) in healthy adult volunteers.

Part B is a multiple-ascending dose design with 3 cohorts (dose levels) in participants with Duchenne.

papers.title: A Study to Assess Vamorolone in Becker Muscular Dystrophy (BMD)
papers.summary:
This Phase II pilot study is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, PK, PD, and exploratory clinical efficacy of vamorolone 500mg (250mg for body weight \<50 kg) daily administered orally compared to placebo over a treatment period of 24 weeks in males with BMD.

Funding Source - FDA OOPD

papers.title: Study of ACE-031 in Subjects With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to determine if ACE-031 is safe and well-tolerated in boys with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) and to select the optimal doses of ACE-031 in terms of safety and pharmacodynamic (PD) activity for designing future studies. \[Note: This study was terminated based on safety data\]

papers.title: Phase 3 Study of Ataluren in Participants With Nonsense Mutation Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (nmDMD)
papers.summary: Dystrophinopathy is a disease continuum that includes Duchenne muscular dystrophy, which develops in boys. It is caused by a mutation in the gene for dystrophin, a protein that is important for maintaining normal muscle structure and function. Loss of dystrophin causes muscle fragility that leads to weakness and loss of walking ability. A specific type of mutation, called a nonsense (premature stop codon) mutation is the cause of dystrophinopathy in approximately 10-15 percent (%) of boys with the disease. Ataluren is an orally delivered, investigational drug that has the potential to overcome

papers.title: Safety and Efficacy of KER-065 in Participants With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), pharmacodynamics (PD), and efficacy of KER-065 administered to adult and pediatric ambulatory and nonambulatory male participants with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) on stable background therapy.

papers.title: Six Month Study of Gentamicin in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy With Stop Codons
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to determine the safety of giving intravenous (IV) gentamicin to boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy who have stop codon mutations.

papers.title: The Effect of Kinesiology Taping on Balance in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary: Investigators investigated that the effects of kinesilogy taping on balance in patients with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy

papers.title: A Study to Assess Vamorolone in Boys With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD)
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to determine whether a new medication called vamorolone is safe and well-tolerated by boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) ages ≥ 4 and \< 7 years old.

papers.title: Long-term, Extension Study of DS-5141b in Patients With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary: This is a multicenter, open-label, long-term, extension, phase 2 study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of long-term treatment with DS-5141b in patients with DMD who have completed DS5141-A-J101.

papers.title: A Study of EDG-5506 in Adult Males With Becker Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary:
The ARCH study was an open-label, single-center, Phase 1b study of sevasemtem (EDG-5506) to assess the safety and pharmacokinetics (PK) of sevasemten in adults with Becker muscular dystrophy (BMD).

Sevasemten is an investigational product intended to protect and improve function of dystrophic muscle fibers.

papers.title: A Study of Tadalafil for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary: The main purpose of this study is to determine if tadalafil can slow the decline in walking ability of boys who have Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD). The study will also assess the safety of tadalafil and any side effects that might be associated with it in boys who have DMD. Participants will receive study treatment (tadalafil or placebo) for the first 48 weeks of the study, and can then continue into an open label extension (OLE) that consists of two periods during which all participants will receive tadalafil. In OLE period 1, all participants will receive tadalafil for 48 weeks. Particip

papers.title: Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of EN001 in Patients With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary: A Multi-center, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled, Phase 1/2 Trial to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of EN001 in Patients with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy

papers.title: Safety Study of Mini-dystrophin Gene to Treat Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to determine the safety of a miniature dystrophin gene in the treatment of progressive muscle weakness due to Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD).

papers.title: A Study in Participants With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Amenable to Exon 44 Skipping to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of ENTR-601-44
papers.summary:
This is a study of the investigational medicine ENTR-601-44 in participants who have Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), a rare genetic condition.

The researchers want to: Test how safe ENTR-601-44 is, learn about any side effects, and look at the potential positive effects of ENTR-601-44, compared to placebo. Placebo looks like the investigational medicine but does not contain any active ingredient. In this summary ENTR-601-44 and placebo are both called study treatments.

The study has 2 parts:

* Part A

  * A Double-Blind Period, to evaluate if ENTR-601-44 is safe and to determine the best

papers.title: Study of Fordadistrogene Movaparvovec in Early Stage Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary: The study will evaluate the safety and dystrophin expression following gene therapy in boys with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD). It is a single-arm, non-randomized, open-label study

papers.title: Efficacy of Stem Cell Therapy in Ambulatory and Non-ambulatory Children With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy - Phase 1-2
papers.summary: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) is a X-linked genetic disorder primarily affecting males, resulting in an absence of dystrophin which ultimately leads to progressive muscle degeneration. Patients with DMD progressively lose functional abilities of movement, breath, and eventually the ability to circulate blood. Currently, there is no cure for DMD, although several strategies are being tested for treatment, none have yet proven to be sufficient. Children with DMD are generally divided into two groups based on severity or progression of the disease, non-ambulatory and ambulatory. Ambulatory pa

papers.title: Efficacy, Safety and Tolerability of Givinostat in Non-ambulant Patients With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary:
This is a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicentre study to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of givinostat in non-ambulant male paediatric (aged 9 to \<18 years) patients with DMD. 138 patients will be randomised 2:1 to givinostat or placebo and will be treated for 18 months.

* Planned screening duration: approximately 4 weeks (±14 days)
* Planned treatment duration: 18 months (approximately 72 weeks)
* Planned follow-up duration: 4 weeks (±7 days) (for patients not participating in the long-term safety study)
* Total duration of study participation: up to 83 w

papers.title: An Efficacy and Safety Trial of Intravenous Zoledronic Acid Twice Yearly in Osteoporotic Children Treated With Glucocorticoids
papers.summary: This study was designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of zoledronic acid compared to placebo in osteoporotic children treated with glucocorticoids

papers.title: Study of Ataluren in Previously Treated Participants With Nonsense Mutation Dystrophinopathy (nmDBMD)
papers.summary:
The objective of this study is to assess the safety and tolerability of 10, 10, 20 milligrams per kilogram (mg/kg) ataluren in participants with nmDBMD who had prior exposure to ataluren in a PTC sponsored clinical trial or treatment plan, and siblings of those participants (provided those participants have completed the placebo-controlled portion of the trial).

The treatment will continue under this protocol until consent withdrawal by participants, withdrawal due to worsen condition after initiating ataluren treatment, withdrawal by investigator, withdrawal due to participant unable to tole

papers.title: Intermittent vs Alternate Daily Regimen of Prednisolone in Ambulatory Boys With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary: The alternate-day regimen is hypothesized to reduce hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis suppression and decrease steroid-related toxicity. Similarly, intermittent regimens aim to provide periodic steroid exposure sufficient for muscle preservation while allowing recovery periods to limit side effects. There is a critical need for localized, prospective data to determine which protocol offers the optimal balance of efficacy and safety for pediatric patients in Pakistan.

papers.title: Tadalafil in Becker Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary: Summary for Patients: This study, funded by the Muscular Dystrophy Association, is intended to build on recent findings published in the journal Nature showing beneficial effects of tadalafil (also known as Cialis) in mice with an animal version of Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophies. Only two doses of tadalafil improved muscle blood flow, allowing the dystrophic mice to perform more exercise with less muscle injury. This new short-term clinical trial will move the testing from animals to human patients with Becker muscular dystrophy and examine the effects of acute tadalafil dosing on mu

papers.title: Transition to Adulthood in People With Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary:
The study will involve boys with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD), from adolescence to adulthood living in Italy, and their families/ caregivers.

The Investigators want to explore patients' mental health, social cognition and perception of body image as well as patients'and caregivers' ability to adapt to changes related to both the disease and various personal and social needs, through the use of short and simple questionnaires, neuropsychological tests and neurocognitive evaluation in ecological scenarios using Virtual Reality. The desire for autonomy and the awareness of both personal and

papers.title: Gentamicin Treatment of Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary:
This study will evaluate the antibiotic gentamicin for treating patients with muscular dystrophy caused by a specific genetic abnormality known as a nonsense mutation. In studies of mice with this type of muscular dystrophy, gentamicin treatment produced positive changes in muscle tissue.

Patients with Duchenne or Becker muscular dystrophy caused by nonsense mutations by may be eligible for this 2-week study. Before starting treatment, patients will have evaluations of muscle strength and general well being. Two muscle tissue samples will be taken by needle biopsy, under local anesthetic and

papers.title: Extension Study of NS-065/NCNP-01 in Boys With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD)
papers.summary: This is an open-label, extension study of NS-065/NCNP-01 administered intravenously once weekly for an additional 192 weeks to boys with DMD who complete Study NS-065/NCNP-01-201.

papers.title: A Study of TAS-205 for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary: The objective of this study is to evaluate the safety and pharmacokinetic of TAS-205 in patients with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.

papers.title: A Study Of PGN-EDO51 In Participants With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Amenable To Exon 51-Skipping Treatment
papers.summary:
The study consists of 3 periods: A Screening Period (up to 45 days), a Multiple Ascending Dose (MAD) Period (16 weeks), and a Long-Term Extension (LTE) Period (108 weeks).

The primary purpose of the MAD period is to evaluate the safety and tolerability of multiple ascending intravenous (IV) doses of PGN-EDO51 administered to participants with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD). The primary purpose of the LTE period is to evaluate the long-term safety and tolerability of PGN-EDO51 in participants who have completed the MAD period.

papers.title: A Study of EDG-5506 in Children With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (LYNX)
papers.summary: The LYNX study is a 2-part, multicenter, Phase 2 study of safety, pharmacokinetics and biomarkers in children with Duchenne muscular dystrophy including a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled part A, followed by an open-label part B.

papers.title: A Double-blind, Escalating Dose, Randomized, Placebo-controlled Study Assessing PK, Safety, Tolerability in Non-ambulant DMD Subjects
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is investigate the pharmacokinetics, safety and tolerability of single subcutaneous administration of GSK2402968 in non-ambulant boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy

papers.title: Phase II Study of NPC-14 (Arbekacin Sulfate) to Explore Safety, Tolerability, and Efficacy in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) is inherited neuromuscular disorders due to mutation in the gene that encodes critical muscle protein called dystrophin. Currently, there is no effective treatment option for the disease. A pharmacological approach by promoting mRNA translation regardless of the presence of premature stop codons by nonsense mutation, called the readthrough strategy, has been developing recently for DMD with nonsense mutation. NPC-14 is a candidate compound for the readthrough strategy, since effective readthrough activities were demonstrated in nonclinical studies. This study

papers.title: A Phase III Double-blind Study With Idebenone in Patients With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) Taking Glucocorticoid Steroids
papers.summary: The purpose of the study is to assess the efficacy of idebenone in delaying the loss of respiratory function in patients with DMD receiving concomitant glucocorticoid steroids

papers.title: Plus Epicatechin Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy in Non-ambulatory Adolescents
papers.summary: This single center open-label pilot study will enroll 15 non-ambulatory children with Duchenne muscular dystrophy at least 8 years of age and who demonstrate pre-clinical cardiomyopathy (defined as a cardiac ejection fraction \>55% with abnormal LV strain by cardiac MRI). They will receive (+)-epicatechin at one of three doses during an 8-week dose-ranging study with assessments at baseline, 2 Weeks, 4weeks, and 8 weeks. The study will determine optimal dosing for future cardiac efficacy studies based on serum / plasma biomarker response using follistatin: myostatin ratio, nitrite/nitrate rati

papers.title: Long-term Safety, Tolerability and Efficacy of Idebenone in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DELPHI Extension)
papers.summary: The scientific aim of the present extension study is to monitor long-term safety and tolerability of idebenone in patients with DMD. Furthermore, the long-term effect on respiratory, cardiac and motor functions, and skeletal muscle strength/function will be assessed.

papers.title: Long-Term Outcomes of Ataluren in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
papers.summary: This study is a long-term study of ataluren in participants with nonsense mutation Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

papers.title: Trial of Cell Based Therapy for DMD
papers.summary: This is a single-center, single-arm, interventional phase 1 trial to evaluate the safety and tolerability of local injection of induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)- derived CD54+ allogeneic muscle progenitor cells in individuals with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD)

papers.title: A Phase I/II, Open Label, Escalating Dose, Pilot Study to Assess Effect, Safety, Tolerability and PK of Multiple SC Doses of Drisapersen in Patients With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy and to Assess the Potential for IV Dosing as an Alternative Route of Administration
papers.summary: The purpose of the extension phase of this study is to determine whether Drisapersen is effective in the treatment of boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy resulting from a mutation thought to be corrected by exon 51 skipping.

papers.title: Open Targets drug and clinical candidates for Duchenne muscular dystrophy
Open Targets drugs acting on DMD
Personalized medicine in the dish to prevent calcium leak associated with short-coupled polymorphic ventricular tachycardia in patient-derived cardiomyocytes.
papers.summary: In patient-derived RyR2-H29D cardiomyocytes modeling short-coupled polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, the Rycal compound S107 most effectively suppressed diastolic sarcoplasmic-reticulum calcium leak, restored calstabin2 binding, and improved contractile homogeneity. Flecainide showed partial calcium-leak benefit, propranolol produced mixed effects, and verapamil failed to prevent the leak and impaired contractility in the mutant model.

papers.title: High-Throughput Screens to Discover Small-Molecule Modulators of Ryanodine Receptor Calcium Release Channels.
papers.summary: The paper validates a time-resolved FRET high-throughput assay for identifying small-molecule modulators of RyR1 in native pig skeletal-muscle sarcoplasmic-reticulum membranes. Five screened compounds reproducibly altered RyR1 structure and activity, with chloroxine showing the desired inhibition at resting calcium and being proposed as a candidate for further testing against sarcoplasmic-reticulum calcium leak.

papers.title: Defective cerebellar ryanodine receptor type 1 and endoplasmic reticulum calcium 'leak' in tremor pathophysiology.
papers.summary: In essential tremor cerebellum, stress-associated remodeling of RyR1, including reduced calstabin1 binding, produced increased endoplasmic-reticulum calcium leak that was attenuated by the RyR1 stabilizer Rycal. The RyR1-S2844D+/+ mouse reproduced increased ER calcium leak, abnormal cerebellar oscillations, and 10-Hz action tremor, while Rycal and dantrolene suppressed the phenotype and caffeine aggravated tremor.

papers.title: Rapamycin inhibits activation of ryanodine receptors from skeletal muscle by the fatty acyl CoA-acyl CoA binding protein complex.
papers.summary: In isolated terminal cisternae from rabbit skeletal muscle, rapamycin abolished fatty acyl-CoA–ACBP-complex-induced calcium efflux and reversed complex-induced calcium release by modifying ryanodine receptor–associated FKBP12. The findings support FKBP12-dependent activation of ryanodine receptor calcium-release channels by fatty acyl-CoA esters.

papers.title: A Mechanism for Statin-Induced Susceptibility to Myopathy.
papers.summary: In human and rat skeletal muscle, statin treatment caused FKBP12 dissociation from RyR1, increased sarcoplasmic-reticulum calcium leak as Ca2+ sparks, and increased pro-apoptotic signaling without measurable skeletal-muscle dysfunction. NOS inhibition, ROS scavenging, inhibition of mitochondrial calcium uptake, and moderate voluntary exercise suppressed the statin-associated RyR1/calcium-leak phenotype.

papers.title: Post-Translational Modifications and Diastolic Calcium Leak Associated to the Novel RyR2-D3638A Mutation Lead to CPVT in Patient-Specific hiPSC-Derived Cardiomyocytes.
papers.summary: In patient-specific cardiomyocytes carrying RYR2-D3638A, catecholaminergic stress increased diastolic sarcoplasmic-reticulum calcium leak and abnormal contractile and electrical activity. The RyR2 stabilizer S107 prevented these abnormalities, whereas metoprolol did not and flecainide improved several outcomes without preventing diastolic leak.

papers.title: Abnormal mannose-6-phosphate receptor trafficking impairs recombinant alpha-glucosidase uptake in Pompe disease fibroblasts.
papers.summary: Patient-derived Pompe disease fibroblasts show an expanded autophagic compartment, particularly in severe and intermediate disease, with CI-MPR increasingly diverted into LC3-positive autophagic or autophagolysosomal compartments. This abnormal trafficking reduces plasma-membrane CI-MPR and recombinant human GAA uptake, while prolonged recombinant human GAA exposure partially restores CI-MPR distribution and GAA activity.

papers.title: Modulation of muscle redox and protein aggregation rescues lethality caused by mutant lamins.
papers.summary: In Drosophila models of LMNA-associated muscular dystrophy, increased autophagy through TOR knockdown or Atg1 overexpression partially suppressed mutant-lamin-associated pupal lethality. Increased p62/Ref(2)P staining was interpreted as evidence of reduced autophagy, while pamoic acid independently improved survival by inhibiting malic enzyme, identifying redox-lowering interventions that may be combined with autophagy enhancement.

papers.title: Impaired Autophagic Flux in Skeletal Muscle of Plectin-Related Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex With Muscular Dystrophy.
papers.summary: Plectin-related epidermolysis bullosa simplex with muscular dystrophy is associated with impaired autophagic clearance in patient muscle, plectin-deficient cells, and muscle-specific plectin-knockout mice. Metformin activated autophagic turnover and partially rescued the cellular flux defect, but its effects in knockout muscle and on protein aggregates or muscle function remain uncertain.

papers.title: Defective autophagy in GNE myopathy is rescued by inhibition of noncanonical Akt-mTORC1 activation across multiple isogenic models.
papers.summary: Across human GNE myopathy cell and organoid models and a Gne-knockout C2C12 model, defective autophagy was linked to noncanonical PI3K–AKT–mTORC1 activation, sustained ULK1 inhibition, and excessive extracellular matrix production. The PI3K inhibitor copanlisib restored ULK1-dependent autophagy and autophagosome formation in vitro, whereas sialic acid supplementation improved sialylation but did not restore autophagic flux.

papers.title: Hydroxyethylamine & phthalimide analogs restoring defects due to GNE dysfunction: rare disease therapeutic significance.
papers.summary: The study found that the hydroxyethylamine–phthalimide analogs LTC-1717 and LTC-181 restored mutant GNE epimerase activity, increased sialic acid content, and improved viability in GNE-deficient skeletal-muscle cells. Both compounds also increased LC3II-based autophagy readouts and reduced the muscle-atrophy marker MuRF1, although the p62 response was not significantly increased and no animal or patient efficacy data were obtained.

papers.title: Exploring ANT1 dysfunction as a pathological driver of wooden breast myopathy in broiler chickens.
papers.summary: In severe wooden breast myopathy, broiler pectoralis major tissue showed reduced ANT1 expression, ATP depletion, metabolic dysregulation, and impaired autophagy, whereas ANT1-deficient C2C12 cells instead exhibited increased autophagy and mitophagy. Rapamycin-enhanced autophagy partially restored ATP and lipid metabolism and shifted atrophy- and differentiation-related gene expression in ANT1-deficient cells, but the study considered the findings preliminary and discordant across the in vivo and in vitro systems.

papers.title: Loss of peroxiredoxin-2 exacerbates eccentric contraction-induced force loss in dystrophin-deficient muscle.
papers.summary: In dystrophin-deficient mdx muscle, eccentric contraction activates a NOX2-dependent reactive oxygen species circuit that rapidly inhibits force but may protect against structural injury. Genetic or pharmacological reduction of this oxidative signaling, including NOX2 deficiency, myoglobin knockout, N-acetylcysteine, and cytoplasmic-actin overexpression, reduced force loss, whereas peroxiredoxin-2 overexpression increased long-term sarcolemmal damage.

papers.title: Rapid, redox-mediated mechanical susceptibility of the cortical microtubule lattice in skeletal muscle.
papers.summary: In dystrophin-deficient mdx skeletal muscle expressing truncated dystrophins, eccentric contraction causes rapid reactive oxygen species-dependent loss of transverse cortical microtubules. N-acetylcysteine completely prevents this loss, whereas the NOX2 inhibitor GSK2795039 provides only partial protection, indicating that ROS from multiple sources contribute.

papers.title: Perturbed Redox Signaling Exacerbates a Mitochondrial Myopathy.
papers.summary: In skeletal muscle-specific Cox15 knockout mice, lowering reactive oxygen species with either Ciona intestinalis alternative oxidase or N-acetylcysteine suppressed compensatory AMPK/PGC-1α signaling, mitochondrial biogenesis, and satellite-cell regeneration, thereby worsening myopathy and reducing survival. The findings indicate that redox-modulating therapies require careful evaluation because physiological ROS signaling can be protective in mitochondrial myopathy.

papers.title: Adaptations to high-intensity interval training in skeletal muscle require NADPH oxidase 2.
papers.summary: In skeletal muscle, acute high-intensity interval exercise transiently increased NOX2-dependent ROS production, while six weeks of high-intensity interval training produced weaker improvements in maximal running capacity, antioxidant defense, glucose-metabolism proteins, and mitochondrial adaptations in NOX2-deficient ncf1* mice than in wild-type mice. The findings identify NOX2-dependent oxidative stress as a signaling mechanism required for selected exercise-training adaptations and provide an experimental model and assays for studying redox-dependent muscle adaptation.

papers.title: Strenuous Acute Exercise Induces Slow and Fast Twitch-Dependent NADPH Oxidase Expression in Rat Skeletal Muscle.
papers.summary: A single strenuous treadmill exercise session produced fiber-type-dependent NADPH oxidase expression and antioxidant responses in rat skeletal muscle. By 24 hours, the authors interpreted the overall response as attenuation of oxidative stress, although their thiol measurements and discussion contain a contradictory statement about the direction of change.

papers.title: Taurine rescues mitochondria-related metabolic impairments in the patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells and epithelial-mesenchymal transition in the retinal pigment epithelium.
papers.summary: In MELAS patient-derived iPSCs carrying the mtDNA A3243G mutation, the paper found increased oxidative stress, impaired mitochondrial respiration, depleted GSH/GSSG ratio, and reduced proliferation and survival; taurine normalized redox measures and rescued these cellular defects. Taurine also reduced nuclear NRF2 accumulation and suppressed epithelial-mesenchymal transition in MELAS iPSC-derived retinal pigment epithelium, providing an experimentally supported oxidative-stress-modulating intervention that may be transferable to diseases such as Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

papers.title: Systemically Administered Homing Peptide Targets Dystrophic Lesions and Delivers Transforming Growth Factor-β (TGFβ) Inhibitor to Attenuate Murine Muscular Dystrophy Pathology.
papers.summary: Systemically administered CAR-DCN, a vascular homing peptide fused to the TGFβ inhibitor decorin, localized to dystrophic muscle lesions and reduced TGFβ signaling, muscle fibrosis, sarcolemmal permeability, and histopathology in muscular dystrophy mouse models. CAR-DCN also improved skeletal-muscle force in mdxDBA2/J mice but did not improve fatigue resistance, respiratory parameters, cardiac outcomes, or fibrosis in abdominal and diaphragm muscle during the three-week study.

papers.title: MST1/2 regulates fibro/adipogenic progenitor fate decisions in skeletal muscle regeneration.
papers.summary: In injured skeletal muscle, FAP-specific Mst1/2 deletion or pharmacological MST1/2 inhibition reduced FAP apoptosis, increased nuclear YAP–Smad2/3 colocalization and myofibroblast differentiation, and increased collagen deposition and Muscle fibrosis. The same perturbation impaired muscle regeneration through reduced IL-6 support of satellite-cell/myoblast proliferation and differentiation, while MST1/2 emerges as a target whose activation may be needed to suppress fibrotic FAP fate decisions.

papers.title: Serum protein and imaging biomarkers after intermittent steroid treatment in muscular dystrophy.
papers.summary: The paper reports that once-weekly glucocorticoid treatment improved muscle strength and reduced fibrosis in the mdx model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy and in sarcoglycan- and dysferlin-mutant models of limb girdle muscular dystrophy. A small open-label pilot of once-weekly prednisone in limb girdle and Becker muscular dystrophy identified treatment-responsive serum proteins and functional trends, but did not directly measure muscle fibrosis and was limited by its size, open-label design, and cohort heterogeneity.

papers.title: Vemurafenib improves muscle histopathology in a mouse model of LAMA2-related congenital muscular dystrophy.
papers.summary: In dyW−/− mice with LAMA2-CMD, short-term vemurafenib reduced Muscle fibrosis and improved selected tibialis anterior histopathology measures while normalizing TGF-β/SMAD3 and mTORC1/p70S6K signaling. The treatment did not improve skeletal muscle strength, prevent muscle loss, restore regenerative capacity, or broadly suppress inflammation, so its functional efficacy was not demonstrated.

papers.title: RUNX2 Activation in Fibro/Adipogenic Progenitors Promotes Muscle Fibrosis in Muscular Dystrophy.
papers.summary: This study identifies a TGF-β1–RUNX2 axis linking macrophage recruitment to fibrogenic differentiation of fibro/adipogenic progenitors (FAPs) in dystrophic muscle, with data in human DMD/LGMD samples and mdx and Dysf-KO mouse models. RUNX2 inhibition with CADD522 reduced muscle fibrosis and improved muscle integrity in mice, while prednisolone reduced inflammatory signaling, RUNX2 activation, fibrosis, and muscle pathology in DMD patients without directly affecting RUNX2 in cultured FAPs.

papers.title: Targeting Galectin-3 to modulate inflammation in LAMA2-deficient congenital muscular dystrophy
papers.summary: This preprint reports that Galectin-3 is upregulated and associated with inflammatory macrophage infiltration in the quadriceps femoris muscle of dyW mice, a model of LAMA2-deficient congenital muscular dystrophy. The Galectin-3 inhibitor TD-139 reduced leukocyte and Galectin-3-positive macrophage infiltration, shifted macrophages toward an anti-inflammatory M2 profile, and decreased fibrosis-related gene expression while increasing muscle-contraction pathways.

papers.title: Nonaminoglycoside compounds induce readthrough of nonsense mutations.
papers.summary: The study identifies two nonaminoglycoside readthrough compounds, RTC#13 and RTC#14, that induce premature-stop-codon readthrough and restore full-length dystrophin protein in mdx mouse myotubes carrying the exon 23 TAA mutation. It also establishes a luciferase-independent protein transcription/translation–ELISA screening assay for discovering readthrough compounds, although the compounds' direct molecular mechanism and therapeutic efficacy in patients remain unresolved.

papers.title: Small molecule Y-320 stimulates ribosome biogenesis, protein synthesis, and aminoglycoside-induced premature termination codon readthrough.
papers.summary: The study shows that combining Y-320 with G418 enhances ribosomal readthrough of premature stop codons in DMD patient-derived myoblasts carrying the DMD E2035X nonsense mutation, increasing dystrophin production 2.2-fold over G418 alone. Y-320 also increases ribosome biogenesis and protein synthesis, and its readthrough-enhancing effect is reduced by CXCR2 antagonism, but the experiments are in vitro and the restored dystrophin level remains low.

papers.title: Gentamicin B1 is a minor gentamicin component with major nonsense mutation suppression activity.
papers.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
papers.summary: The paper shows that the minor gentamicin component gentamicin B1 is a potent inducer of premature termination codon readthrough, unlike the major pharmaceutical gentamicin components. B1 induced readthrough in cultured cells carrying nonsense mutations in DMD and other genes and in an in vivo tumor xenograft model, but the paper notes variable B1 content in pharmaceutical gentamicin and suppression of B1 activity by major gentamicins.

papers.title: 2,6-Diaminopurine Induces ACTN3 Premature Termination Codon Readthrough.
papers.summary: In transfected HEK293 cells, 2,6-diaminopurine induced ribosomal readthrough of the ACTN3 R577X premature termination codon at micromolar concentrations and enabled production of full-length α-actinin-3. Readthrough-derived α-actinin-3 formed more homodimers than protein derived from the ACTN3 577R allele, suggesting potential functional restoration, but functional recovery in humans or athletes was not tested.

papers.title: Higher throughput drug screening for rare respiratory diseases: readthrough therapy in primary ciliary dyskinesia.
papers.summary: The paper establishes an expandable, miniaturized patient-derived nasal epithelial air–liquid interface platform for screening premature-stop-codon therapies in primary ciliary dyskinesia. In MCIDAS-associated reduced generation of motile cilia, gentamicin and ataluren combined with nonsense-mediated decay inhibition restored MCIDAS expression and basal-body formation, but did not restore motile cilia.

papers.title: Synergy between Readthrough and Nonsense Mediated Decay Inhibition in a Murine Model of Cystic Fibrosis Nonsense Mutations.
papers.summary: In primary intestinal organoids and airway epithelial cultures from G542X-Cftr mice, inhibition of nonsense-mediated decay with SMG1i synergized with G418-, gentamicin-, and paromomycin-mediated ribosomal readthrough to restore functional CFTR. The benefit was context-dependent: SMG1i alone, NMDI-14, amlexanox, PTC124, escin, tobramycin, and amikacin did not produce a complementary functional rescue, and toxicity at higher combination doses limited the strongest responses.

unread.title: Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: Describes approved and clinical-stage approaches that restore dystrophin or address secondary disease pathology and provides established diagnostic and multidisciplinary management guidance for DMD.

unread.title: Entries in the Leiden Duchenne muscular dystrophy mutation database: an overview of mutation types and paradoxical cases that confirm the reading-frame rule.
unread.why: The Leiden DMD mutation database provides a substantial variant resource, and the study evaluates the reading-frame rule as a genotype-phenotype framework applicable to DMD and Becker muscular dystrophy.

unread.title: Clinical Manifestations and Overall Management Strategies for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.
unread.why: Reports established DMD management strategies addressing progressive weakness, contractures, respiratory failure, sleep apnea, and cardiomyopathy.

unread.title: Optimization of antisense-mediated exon skipping for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: Reviews established DMD exon-skipping therapies and transferable design and delivery methods for improving applicability and multi-exon skipping.

unread.title: Golodirsen for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: Summarizes the pharmacology, efficacy, safety, and applicability of golodirsen, an approved antisense therapy for approximately 8% of exon-53-amenable DMD patients.

unread.title: Casimersen for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: Reports preclinical and clinical data for casimersen, an accelerated-approved antisense therapy that skips exon 45 and is applicable to roughly 8% of patients with DMD.

unread.title: Medical management of muscle weakness in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: Provides expert consensus recommendations for using deflazacort, weekend prednisone, and eteplirsen in the medical management of DMD muscle weakness.

unread.title: Therapeutic developments for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: Reviews approved and clinical-stage DMD therapeutic modalities that restore partially functional dystrophin or target disease-related pathways.

unread.title: Genotype-phenotype analysis in 2,405 patients with a dystrophinopathy using the UMD-DMD database: a model of nationwide knowledgebase.
unread.why: This same-disease study presents a large curated dystrophinopathy database, diagnostic and mutation-analysis resources, and a tool for predicting eligibility for deletion 45–53 exon skipping.

unread.title: Mutational spectrum of DMD mutations in dystrophinopathy patients: application of modern diagnostic techniques to a large cohort.
unread.why: This large DMD cohort provides mutation data, modern diagnostic approaches, and estimates of the fraction of patients eligible for antisense exon-skipping therapies.

unread.title: Mutation spectrum of the dystrophin gene in 442 Duchenne/Becker muscular dystrophy cases from one Japanese referral center.
unread.why: This study establishes a high-quality Japanese dystrophinopathy database and demonstrates a complementary diagnostic workflow with successful mutation detection in all 442 cases.

unread.title: Analysis of Dp71 contribution in the severity of mental retardation through comparison of Duchenne and Becker patients differing by mutation consequences on Dp71 expression.
unread.why: The large DMD/BMD cohort supplies molecular and clinical data showing that Dp71 expression and mutation location can stratify cognitive-impairment severity.

unread.title: Protein- and mRNA-based phenotype-genotype correlations in DMD/BMD with point mutations and molecular basis for BMD with nonsense and frameshift mutations in the DMD gene.
unread.why: The study developed a nearly complete diagnostic strategy for small DMD mutations and provides mRNA, protein, and phenotype data that distinguish DMD and BMD mechanisms.

unread.title: Point mutations at the carboxy terminus of the human dystrophin gene: implications for an association with mental retardation in DMD patients.
unread.why: The study applies PCR-SSCP to detect DMD-associated C-terminal point mutations and provides data linking disruption of the Dp71 and Dp116 isoforms to cognitive outcomes.

unread.title: The identification of point mutations in Duchenne muscular dystrophy patients by using reverse-transcription PCR and the protein truncation test.
unread.why: This DMD study demonstrates a mutation-screening assay that identified point mutations and small insertions or deletions in patients without large deletions.

unread.title: A comprehensive database of Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophy patients (0-18 years old) in East China.
unread.why: The linked clinical, genetic, treatment, cardiac, and respiratory registry of 194 DMD and 35 BMD patients provides a reusable recruitment and natural-history resource.

unread.title: Point mutations in the dystrophin gene: evidence for frequent use of cryptic splice sites as a result of splicing defects.
unread.why: The study establishes a protocol for experimentally determining splice defects and their translational consequences in DMD.

unread.title: DGGE-based whole-gene mutation scanning of the dystrophin gene in Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophy patients.
unread.why: The validated 95-amplicon DGGE assay detected known and novel dystrophin variants in DMD/BMD patients and carriers, demonstrating a reusable diagnostic method.

unread.title: Measurement of the clinical utility of a combined mutation detection protocol in carriers of Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: The combined protocol achieved high mutation detection in DMD/BMD pedigrees and improved carrier classification over conventional testing.

unread.title: A population-based study of dystrophin mutations in Canada.
unread.why: The study provides a large mutation and clinical dataset from 773 dystrophinopathy patients and supports standardized diagnostic approaches.

unread.title: A single NGS-based assay covering the entire genomic sequence of the DMD gene facilitates diagnostic and newborn screening confirmatory testing.
unread.why: The assay covered the complete 2.2-Mb DMD gene, detected copy-number and sequence variants in index cases and carriers, and was concordant with other methods.

unread.title: Exon-skipping therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: This review summarizes an existing DMD therapy that converts out-of-frame mutations into in-frame mutations and has demonstrated efficacy in mouse and dog models with clinical trials underway.

unread.title: New variants, challenges and pitfalls in DMD genotyping: implications in diagnosis, prognosis and therapy.
unread.why: The study combines detailed molecular diagnostic methods with a patient registry to identify mutations and candidates for mutation-centered therapies.

unread.title: Cardiac MRI biomarkers for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: The review identifies cardiac MRI measures of function, fibrosis, strain, edema, and fat that can serve as earlier DMD cardiac involvement and therapy-evaluation biomarkers.

unread.title: The role of muscle biopsy in analysis of the dystrophin gene in Duchenne muscular dystrophy: experience of a national referral centre.
unread.why: The referral-center study detected 79 mutations in 89 DMD samples using muscle-biopsy transcript analysis and validated a sensitive nondeletion mutation-screening protocol.

unread.title: Clinical and molecular characterization of a cohort of patients with novel nucleotide alterations of the Dystrophin gene detected by direct sequencing.
unread.why: Reports a validated diagnostic strategy for identifying and characterizing small, nonsense, and splice-altering DMD mutations in a DMD/BMD cohort.

unread.title: Comprehensive genetic characteristics of dystrophinopathies in China.
unread.why: Provides a large DMD/BMD registry and mutation database while identifying patient subgroups potentially eligible for stop-codon read-through and exon-skipping therapies.

unread.title: Mutation analysis in a population-based cohort of boys with Duchenne or Becker muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: Provides population-based evidence for diagnostic mutation testing strategies in boys with DMD/BMD and quantifies the yield of deletion, duplication, and point-mutation testing.

unread.title: Rapid and cost effective detection of small mutations in the DMD gene by high resolution melting curve analysis.
unread.why: Validates high-resolution melting curve analysis as a low-cost screening method for small DMD mutations before sequencing in patients and female carriers.

unread.title: Consecutive analysis of mutation spectrum in the dystrophin gene of 507 Korean boys with Duchenne/Becker muscular dystrophy in a single center.
unread.why: Reports a large DMD/BMD cohort analyzed with combined deletion/duplication and sequencing methods, generating a regional mutation resource for molecular trials.

unread.title: Strategy for comprehensive molecular testing for Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophies.
unread.why: Establishes a tiered molecular testing strategy that achieved 98% causal-mutation detection in patients suspected of having DMD.

unread.title: Simultaneous MLPA-based multiplex point mutation and deletion analysis of the dystrophin gene.
unread.why: Demonstrates a multiplex MLPA assay that combines DMD deletion/duplication detection with screening for common point mutations in one test.

unread.title: Mutation analysis of the dystrophin gene in Southern French DMD or BMD families: from Southern blot to protein truncation test.
unread.why: Reports a long-term diagnostic workflow achieving at least 86% detection of DMD point mutations using transcript-based and PCR-based methods.

unread.title: Genetic profile of Brazilian patients with dystrophinopathies.
unread.why: Provides a comprehensive Brazilian DMD/BMD cohort and a combined MLPA/NGS workflow for characterizing mutations relevant to mutation-specific treatment planning.

unread.title: Non-isotopic analysis of single strand conformation polymorphism (SSCP) in the exon 13 region of the human dystrophin gene.
unread.why: Demonstrates PCR followed by non-isotopic SSCP and sequencing for detecting an exon 13 DMD point mutation in patients without large rearrangements.

unread.title: One hundred twenty-one dystrophin point mutations detected from stored DNA samples by combinatorial denaturing high-performance liquid chromatography.
unread.why: Validates a cost-effective pooled denaturing HPLC and sequencing strategy for detecting small DMD mutations in stored DNA samples.

unread.title: Small mutation screening in the DMD gene by whole exome sequencing of an argentine Duchenne/Becker muscular dystrophies cohort.
unread.why: Applies whole-exome sequencing to identify DMD small mutations, identify 15 Ataluren candidates, and diagnose alternative limb-girdle dystrophy in biopsy-positive cases.

unread.title: A Comprehensive Analysis of 2013 Dystrophinopathies in China: A Report From National Rare Disease Center.
unread.why: Establishes a large, prospectively followed Chinese dystrophinopathy registry with clinical, treatment, mutation, and serum-index data useful for DMD research.

unread.title: The discovery of the DNA methylation episignature for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: Reports a blood-based DMD-specific DNA methylation episignature and validates its specificity against other neurodevelopmental disorders, providing a candidate diagnostic biomarker.

unread.title: Gene editing and modulation for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: Synthesizes clinically advanced and experimental gene-restoration strategies for DMD, including AAV delivery, splice modulation, and genome editing.

unread.title: Theragnosis for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.
unread.why: Validates a 97%-sensitive molecular diagnostic and theragnostic workflow in 400 patients and identifies mutation-specific eligibility for exon-skipping and readthrough therapies.

unread.title: Higher Prevalence of Nonsense Pathogenic DMD Variants in a Single-Center Cohort from Brazil: A Genetic Profile Study That May Guide the Choice of Disease-Modifying Treatments.
unread.why: Provides a regional DMD genetic profile and a reusable MLPA/NGS workflow for identifying nonsense variants that may qualify for mutation-specific disease-modifying drugs.

unread.title: Perspectives on the advances in the pharmacotherapeutic management of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: Surveys established and investigational pharmacotherapies for DMD, including corticosteroids and drugs targeting inflammation, fibrosis, and dystrophin replacement.

unread.title: Novel mutations of dystrophin gene in DMD patients detected by rapid scanning in biplex exons DHPLC analysis.
unread.why: Reports a faster, lower-cost biplex-exon DHPLC protocol that detected new point mutations in four DMD patients negative for large rearrangements.

unread.title: Current Concepts in the Orthopaedic Management of Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.
unread.why: Synthesizes reusable nonsurgical and operative management strategies for DMD-related scoliosis and their effects on sitting balance, comfort, respiratory function, and survival.

unread.title: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension in a child with Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: Provides DMD-specific safety data showing that deflazacort can cause morbid obesity and idiopathic intracranial hypertension, informing monitoring of an existing treatment.

unread.title: [Nonsense readthrough therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy].
unread.why: Reports amelioration of muscular dystrophy with arbekacin-mediated nonsense readthrough and describes clinical testing of arbekacin alongside gentamicin and PTC124.

unread.title: Emerging therapies for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: This review synthesizes clinical and preclinical data for multiple reusable DMD treatments and identifies sensitive biomarkers, natural-history data, and improved trial designs as development resources.

unread.title: Viltolarsen for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: The paper summarizes preclinical and clinical evidence for viltolarsen, an existing exon-53-skipping antisense therapy applicable to a defined DMD genotype subset.

unread.title: Emerging genetic therapies to treat Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: This review reports dystrophin restoration and completed phase I safety results for genotype-directed nonsense-codon suppression and exon-skipping therapies in DMD.

unread.title: Update on the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: This review describes tested DMD treatment strategies spanning gene replacement, exon skipping, mutation suppression, cell therapy, and pharmacological cardiac care, with supporting translational evidence.

unread.title: Therapeutic Strategies for Dystrophin Replacement in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.
unread.why: The paper reviews in-vitro and in-vivo approaches for restoring dystrophin in DMD, providing reusable therapeutic concepts and experimental implementations.

unread.title: A Single Lipid Nanoparticle Formulation Enables Delivery of Diverse RNA Therapeutics to Human Muscle Models of Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
unread.why: The study establishes a broadly reusable RNA-delivery platform across multiple human DMD muscle models and demonstrates dystrophin restoration and utrophin upregulation with diverse RNA cargos.

unread.title: RNA trans-splicing treatment for Duchenne muscular dystrophy
unread.why: The study develops a scar-free AAV strategy for delivering full-length or mini-dystrophin and reports preservation of muscle structure and function in vivo.

unread.title: Axonopathy in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy limits microdystrophin gene therapy efficacy
unread.why: Using the mdx model, the study identifies DMD-related peripheral nerve pathology and supplies mechanistic evidence that muscle-restricted microdystrophin requires complementary neural targeting to restore motor-unit function.

unread.title: AAV and lentiviral transduction in Duchenne muscular dystrophy cardiomyocytes activate cell stress responses
unread.why: The work provides DMD cardiomyocyte models and transcriptomic evidence identifying cell-cycle and p53 stress responses induced by viral gene-transfer vectors.

unread.title: Compact adenine base editors to enable therapeutic rescue of Duchenne muscular dystrophy
unread.why: The study engineers compact single-vector adenine base editors and demonstrates therapeutically relevant exon 45 and 51 skipping in human DMD muscle cells.

unread.title: Elimination of intramuscular immunoglobin accumulation alleviates Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
unread.why: The study identifies intramuscular IgG accumulation as a DMD disease accelerator and shows sustained disease benefit from B-cell depletion in two mouse models.

unread.title: FDA-approved antisense oligonucleotide therapies for duchenne muscular dystrophy: current status and future outlook.
unread.why: This review consolidates pivotal, post-marketing, and follow-up evidence for four approved DMD exon-skipping therapies and their genotype-specific applicability and clinical limitations.

unread.title: Case Report: The effect of early initiation of eteplirsen treatment on the cardiac and motor disease course in an individual with Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: This DMD case provides direct longitudinal evidence that early eteplirsen plus enalapril was associated with five years of stable cardiac function and motor status.

unread.title: Givinostat enhances antisense oligonucleotide efficacy in the <i>mdx52</i> model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: The study directly validates a givinostat–ASO combination in an exon 52 DMD model and mutant human myoblasts, with improved skipping, dystrophin restoration, muscle histology, and force.

unread.title: A Registry-Based Perspective of Interventional Clinical Trials for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.
unread.why: The paper curates and characterizes 232 interventional DMD trials, providing a reusable registry resource for identifying DMD therapies and trial designs.

unread.title: LTBP4 genotype predicts age of ambulatory loss in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: The cohort identifies LTBP4 genotype as a practical prognostic biomarker for age at loss of ambulation and provides a mechanistic TGF-beta signaling basis for the modifier effect.

unread.title: Histological effects of givinostat in boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: This phase II study shows that at least 12 months of givinostat increased muscle tissue and reduced fibrosis, necrosis, and fatty replacement in boys with DMD.

unread.title: Safety and efficacy of givinostat in boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (EPIDYS): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
unread.why: This large randomized phase III trial directly evaluates a clinically deployable givinostat treatment regimen in DMD using a motor-function endpoint.

unread.title: A novel chemical-combination screen in zebrafish identifies epigenetic small molecule candidates for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: The authors identify and independently validate the HDAC-inhibitor combination oxamflatin plus salermide as improving skeletal-muscle structure in a DMD zebrafish model.

unread.title: Targeting HDAC8 to ameliorate skeletal muscle differentiation in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: The study identifies elevated HDAC8 in DMD and shows that selective HDAC8 inhibition rescues skeletal-muscle defects comparably to givinostat.

unread.title: Preclinical studies in the mdx mouse model of duchenne muscular dystrophy with the histone deacetylase inhibitor givinostat.
unread.why: This dose-ranging mdx study provides preclinical efficacy and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic evidence supporting givinostat translation into DMD trials.

unread.title: Exome Sequencing and Optical Genome Mapping in Molecularly Unsolved Cases of Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy: Identification of a Causative X-Chromosomal Inversion Disrupting the DMD Gene.
unread.why: The study demonstrates that WES followed by optical genome mapping identifies a large DMD-disrupting inversion missed by routine testing and shows the diagnostic utility of long-read confirmation.

unread.title: Predictors of Loss of Ambulation in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
unread.why: This DMD meta-analysis identifies prognostic indicators of loss of ambulation and provides outcome-measure and natural-history evidence that glucocorticoids delay ambulation loss.

unread.title: Considering the Promise of Vamorolone for Treating Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.
unread.why: The article evaluates clinical and preclinical vamorolone data showing efficacy similar to conventional glucocorticoids with potentially fewer adverse effects in DMD.

unread.title: Predictors of cardiac disease in duchenne muscular dystrophy: a systematic review and evidence grading.
unread.why: This DMD review provides graded patient-level evidence for cardioprotective drugs, cardiac outcomes, and genotype-based cardiac risk predictors.

unread.title: Good response to the late treatment with ataluren in a boy with Duchenne muscular dystrophy: could the previous mild course of the disease have affected the outcome?
unread.why: This DMD case report provides direct patient-level evidence that late ataluren treatment was associated with two years of functional stability and declining creatine kinase.

unread.title: Epigenetic small molecule screening identifies a new HDACi compound for ameliorating Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: An epigenetic compound screen in DMD zebrafish identified SR-4370 and showed that treatment reduced muscle degeneration and increased lifespan.

unread.title: Eteplirsen for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
unread.why: This randomized placebo-controlled DMD trial directly showed that eteplirsen induced dystrophin and improved or stabilized ambulation in patients eligible for exon 51 skipping.

unread.title: Genotype and phenotype characterization in a large dystrophinopathic cohort with extended follow-up.
unread.why: The 320-patient extended-follow-up study provides mutation-stratified natural-history data and clinically useful endpoints for DMD/BMD trial design.

unread.title: Rapid direct sequence analysis of the dystrophin gene.
unread.why: The paper develops and validates a rapid, economical method for directly sequencing the large dystrophin gene, including mutations missed by deletion testing.

unread.title: The Genetic Landscape of Dystrophin Mutations in Italy: A Nationwide Study.
unread.why: The 1,902-patient national study provides a substantial genotype resource and quantifies the proportion of patients potentially eligible for mutation-directed therapies.

unread.title: Cardiac Dysfunction in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Is Less Frequent in Patients With Mutations in the Dystrophin Dp116 Coding Region Than in Other Regions.
unread.why: Longitudinal DMD data identify Dp116 expression as a cardiac involvement biomarker and validate echocardiographic cardiac outcomes.

unread.title: Comprehensive analysis for genetic diagnosis of Dystrophinopathies in Japan.
unread.why: The Remudy dataset characterizes 1,497 patients and supplies a phenotype-linked mutation reference for DMD/BMD diagnosis and treatment development.
